## Benchmark Results: .NET 9 vs .NET 10

**TextAnalyzer** — 3 methods, 1M iterations each, Release build, ~50-word input text.

| Method | .NET 9 (ns/op) | .NET 10 (ns/op) | Trend |
|--------|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| `AverageWordLength` | 647–1100 | 394–779 | ✅ ~30-40% faster |
| `WordLengthHistogram` | 1169–2034 | 1181–1949 | ➖ ~comparable |
| `UniqueWordCount` | 5975–6843 | 3892–7568 | ➖ ~comparable (noisy) |

**Note:** This machine is under significant load from other processes, causing high variance between runs. The absolute numbers should be taken with a grain of salt, but directionally:

- **`AverageWordLength`** shows a consistent improvement on .NET 10 (likely due to loop/arithmetic optimizations).
- **`WordLengthHistogram`** and **`UniqueWordCount`** show no significant regression or improvement — differences are within noise.

**Conclusion:** The .NET 9 → 10 upgrade appears safe from a performance standpoint for these methods. No regressions detected; `AverageWordLength` may benefit from JIT improvements in .NET 10.

The benchmark project is at `TextAnalyzer.Benchmarks/` if you want to re-run on a quieter machine for more precise numbers.
